newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Orbotech target price up.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Orbotech target price up.

text.p: Lehman Brothers raised its one-year price target for Orbotech to $42-$45 a share and said there was upside to its second-quarter earnings per share (EPS) estimate.
In June Lehman raised its price target to $38-$40. Orbotech closed at $36-1/2 on Monday.
The Israeli maker of automated optical inspection equipment for the printed circuit board industry will report second quarter results on August 4.

"We believe the company stands a good chance of beating our second-quarter EPS estimate of $0.49 (up 29 percent). Indeed, we could easily see EPS in the $0.52-$0.53 range," analyst Ted Kundtz said in a report.

""We will be reviewing our current 1997 EPS estimate of $1.99 (up 29 percent year over year) and $2.35 forecast (up 18 percent) for 1998 following the second quarter release and, in all likelihood, will be moving these numbers higher."
Last week Orbotech announced it has agreed to purchase 51 percent of Germany's W.Schuh GmbH.

"We estimate Schuh could generate $7-$8 million in sales in 1997, representing growth in excess of 30 percent. Orbotech believes Schuh can contribute $10-$11 million in sales next year and make a modest EPS contribution," the report said, adding there was potential for a signficiant profit contribution in 1999.
Lehman maintained its 1-Buy rating for the shares.
